answer: To limit sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each account to lock scarce tokens before it can submit work, then slash the stake when independently checked results fail a challenge. A grove of honest agents can randomly audit claims, while an oasis of new identities gains no voting weight until its stake survives several rounds. An attacker must therefore tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it, making mass identities costly rather than free. An onyx badge alone should not count as proof: copied credentials do not replace the locked stake.
